applicability: End-to-end additive one-way audio latency budget checked against the ITU-T G.114 recommended 150 ms conversational-quality threshold
assumptions: each stage delay is a fixed, declared value rather than a measured statistical distribution
the components are additive with no overlap or pipelining between stages
one-way (not round-trip) latency is the relevant quantity
excluded: adaptive jitter-buffer behavior under real network conditions
uncertainty: Plain arithmetic sum checked against the well-known ITU-T G.114 150 ms one-way conversational-quality guideline; hand-verified before use (20+20+40+60+5+10=155 ms, exceeding 150 ms by 5 ms).
limits_policy: Total latency exceeding 150 ms is flagged rather than accepted, but the guideline's applicability to non-conversational use cases is explicitly disclosed as unresolved.
